title: Credit Control Basis: The Late Charge Rate Carried into a Catering Closure
content:
## The rate

How long a client has gone without paying anything, and whether anything is still owed, set the late charge rate carried into the closure of a Corporate Catering Service Agreement.

**Where the most recent payment entry on the agreement fell more than 60 days before the day it closes and an amount stands unsettled on it**, the late charge is twice — 2 times — the monthly late percentage printed against the catering service level.

**Where the most recent payment entry fell more than 30 but not more than 60 days before that day and an amount stands unsettled on it**, the late charge is that monthly late percentage printed against the catering service level, taken once — 1 time.

**Otherwise**, no late charge is carried.

## Judgement points

*Both conditions on each branch are tested together.* An agreement whose most recent payment entry fell 90 days before the closing day but which carries nothing unsettled sits on the third branch and carries no late charge.

*The boundaries.* A most recent payment entry exactly 60 days before the closing day is not more than 60 days before it, so it falls on the second branch; at 61 days it falls on the first. A most recent payment entry exactly 30 days before the closing day is not more than 30 days before it, so it falls on the third branch and carries no late charge; at 31 days it falls on the second.

| Days between the most recent payment entry and the day the agreement closes | An amount stands unsettled | The rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| More than 60 | yes | twice the monthly late percentage printed against the service level |
| More than 30 and not more than 60 | yes | the monthly late percentage printed against the service level |
| 30 or fewer | yes | none |
| Any | no | none |

*Illustration.* Where the monthly late percentage printed against the catering service level is 1.25 per cent, an agreement carrying an unsettled amount whose most recent payment entry fell 75 days before the closing day carries a rate of 2.5 per cent; one whose most recent payment entry fell 45 days before that day carries 1.25 per cent.
